editorial:
You meet Jodi, a teen who towers over everyone and has spent years hiding her height. The movie follows her awkward school life, friendships, and crushes as she slowly learns to stop shrinking herself. It has a light, teen-comedy feel with some heartfelt moments, so you get laughs and a little emotional payoff without anything too heavy. The high school setting keeps everything familiar and easy to follow.

The acting is warm and easy to watch, and the pacing keeps things moving from scene to scene, though some jokes feel familiar and the story can be predictable. If you enjoy coming-of-age rom-coms, you will likely have fun with its sweet message.  It is not groundbreaking, but it delivers a cozy, feel-good watch for a relaxed night.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Jodi stops hiding and owns her height, especially during the school dance and her big moment with Jack. The twist is that the guy she chased is not the one who truly sees her; instead, her longtime friend Dunkleman has been the better match all along. She chooses confidence over chasing approval, and the movie ends with her standing tall and happy.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves teen rom-coms and underdog stories.
